title: A/B Testing (Route-level) — Console screens notes, edge cases, copy/terminology
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture working notes from design/eng collaboration on the route-level A/B testing Console screens.
- Focus: edge cases (paused experiments, overlapping rollouts, capacity/fallback interactions), terminology/copy alternatives, and UI guardrail/warning states.
- This is not a full spec (see DES-142 / design spec in Confluence). This is the “stuff that comes up in reviews”.

Attendees / input sources
- Design: Kenji (workflow), Tessa (overall)
- PM: Marissa (feature), Paula (telemetry requirements)
- Eng: Dylan (lead), Chloe (backend), Jada (framework), Allison (observability), Sean (SRE)
- Notes from: internal dogfood feedback thread (eng), SRE guardrail email, support confusion reports around “control” semantics.

Glossary (current terms vs alternatives)
- Experiment: top-level object. Alternate: “Traffic split”. (PM preference: “Experiment” matches eval harness & reporting).
- Variant: A and B (or more). Alternate: “Treatment”, “Candidate”, “Model config”.
- Control: NOT always true. We may not be doing “control vs treatment”; can be “Model vX vs vY” or “same model w/ different params”. Strong suggestion: don’t label anything as “Control” by default. Allow optional “Baseline” tag.
- Route: “API route” in UI. Example: /v1/chat/completions. Need to clarify: this is a Redwood Console “Route” concept (project route / endpoint) not necessarily the literal HTTP path in all cases.
- Exposure: a request that was eligible for experiment and got assigned a variant. Keep this term mostly internal; in UI consider “Assigned requests” or “Eligible requests”.
- Assignment key: hash inputs (tenant + key + optional user header). In UI: “Stickiness key” (preferred) but we must be careful: it’s not guaranteed unless customer provides stable identifier.

Open questions (tracked separately, but captured here)
- Do we allow >2 variants in Beta UI? Backend supports N variants; design currently shows 2 with “Add variant” button gated by feature flag.
- Do we show scheduling (start/end) in Beta? Likely yes but with minimal controls.
- Do we allow “Paused” state distinct from “Stopped”? Proposed: yes, but only for “Stop without deleting” + ability to resume with same config.

Screen-by-screen notes

1) Experiments list view
What we need
- Row info: Name, Route, Status (Draft/Running/Paused/Stopped/Archived), Split summary (e.g., A 90% / B 10%), Created by, Last modified.
- Quick actions: View, Stop, Resume, Roll back (if we support “rollback” as a special action), Duplicate.

Copy/UX notes
- Status: “Paused” means config preserved, traffic = 0% (all traffic goes to default route policy). “Stopped” is ambiguous; prefer “Ended”.
- “Archived” vs “Deleted”: we should never hard-delete; rename to “Archived” and keep audit trail.

Edge cases
- Experiment exists but route no longer exists or route renamed.
  - UI: show “Route missing” badge; block Start/Resume.
- User lacks permissions to stop/start.
  - UI: action disabled + tooltip “Requires Project Admin”.
- Overlapping experiments on same route.
  - Backend likely prevents (validation) but list may show “Conflict” if two are configured due to legacy/bug.

2) Create experiment flow (DES-142)
Flow (proposed)
- Step 1: Basics
  - Experiment name
  - Project selector (if not already scoped)
  - Route selector
- Step 2: Variants
  - Variant A: model + config
  - Variant B: model + config
  - Traffic split
  - Stickiness key selection (or display of default assignment behavior)
- Step 3: Measurement
  - Metrics included by default (latency, TTFT, error rate, tokens, cost)
  - Optional: attach eval suite (if enabled)
- Step 4: Review & Validate
  - Validate button (runs backend validation)
  - Summary of warnings/errors
  - Start experiment

Copy suggestions (names & guidance)
- “Traffic split” vs “Allocation”
  - Recommendation: “Traffic split” in UI; “allocation” in tooltips.
- “Stickiness” section
  - Header: “Consistent assignment (stickiness)”
  - Helper text: “Requests are deterministically assigned to a variant based on a stable identifier. To keep the same end-user on the same variant, provide a stable user identifier header (recommended).”
  - Avoid implying cookie-based behavior.
- Model config labels
  - “Model” + “Serving config” (temperature, max tokens, system prompt override if any) should be shown; avoid “Prompt” label unless we actually capture prompt changes.

Validation + warnings (important)
- Blocking errors (cannot start)
  - Route already has a running experiment
  - Invalid split totals (must sum to 100)
  - Variant config invalid / model not available in region
  - Missing entitlements (Dedicated-only features, etc.)
- Non-blocking warnings (can start, but show strong warning)
  - No stable stickiness key configured -> “Variant may flip across requests; results may be noisy.”
  - Split includes <5% variant -> “Small allocations may take longer to reach statistical confidence.”
  - Variant B capacity risk (if Dedicated pool constrained) -> “May increase 429/5xx; consider guardrails.”

Design note: where to show warnings
- During “Validate” step show consolidated warnings.
- ALSO inline warnings on Step 2 (Variants) if we can compute cheaply (e.g., split too small, stickiness missing).

3) Experiment detail view (while Running)
Tabs
- Overview (status, split, route)
- Results
- Configuration
- Audit log

Overview content
- Current split summary with “Edit split” (if we allow mid-flight edits). (Eng note: edits require new revision + audit event; results should show by revision boundary?)
- Guardrails status card: “Healthy” / “At risk” / “Rolled back”.
- Recent alerts (link to dashboards).

Copy/UX: the STOP button
- Use “End experiment” instead of “Stop”.
- Confirmation modal text: 
  - Title: “End experiment?”
  - Body: “Traffic will return to the route’s default policy. Results remain available. You can resume later.”
  - Buttons: “End experiment” (primary) / “Cancel”
- For “Pause”: 
  - Title: “Pause experiment?”
  - Body: “Temporarily set split to 0%. Configuration is preserved.”

Operational edge cases
- Auto-rollback triggered by guardrail evaluator
  - Status should transition to “Rolled back” (separate from Ended). This is valuable for audit/reconstruction.
  - UI should show: when it rolled back, which guardrail triggered (latency p95, error rate, 429s), and link to runbook.
- Partial region issues
  - Experiment is defined for route+project, but traffic is multi-region.
  - We need a region filter in Results; Overview should show “Regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1”.

4) Results dashboard (DES-143) — display decisions
Core comparisons
- Time series and summary cards for:
  - Request volume (eligible/assigned)
  - Error rate (4xx, 5xx, timeouts; decide if 429 is separate)
  - Latency (p50/p95/p99), TTFT for streaming
  - Tokens per request (input/output)
  - Cost per request / per 1K tokens (if we can compute)

Terminology notes
- Prefer “Request latency” (end-to-end) and “Time to first token” (TTFT) as separate metrics.
- “Cost” needs a tooltip: “Estimated cost based on token and GPU attribution. May differ from invoice totals.”

Confidence/Stats indicators
- Strong concern from ML: avoid implying statistical significance without enough data.
- Proposal:
  - Show a simple “Data quality” / “Sufficient sample size” indicator.
  - Use “Directional” language: “Variant B appears faster (p95 -12ms) over selected window” without “significant” claims unless we have a clear test.
  - If we do show p-values/CI, hide behind “Advanced” section with disclaimers.

Quality metrics integration (optional in Beta)
- If eval suite attached, show:
  - Latest eval run date
  - Score delta (B - A) with CI if available
  - Link to full eval report
- Copy: “Offline evals reflect the attached prompt set and do not measure production user satisfaction.”

Filters and drill-down
- Minimum filters: time range, region, variant, status (exclude time after rollback?), model.
- Drill-down: sample requests? (likely NO for privacy; at most show aggregate + “View in tracing” if customer has tracing enabled.)

Important edge cases for results
- Experiment paused/resumed
  - Graph should annotate state changes (vertical markers).
  - If paused, variant traffic should go to zero; results should not average across the whole period without noting inactive segments.
- Split changed mid-flight
  - Same annotation needed.
- Overlapping rollouts/canaries
  - If canary is also active for the same route, precedence rules matter. UI should show “Other routing policies active” banner.
  - Banner text (draft): “This route has other rollout policies active (canary/fallback). Experiment assignments may be overridden for reliability.”

5) Configuration tab
What to show
- Read-only JSON-ish summary of current config (model IDs, parameters, split, eligibility rules, stickiness inputs, sampling rates for exposure logs)
- “Edit” action should create a new revision.

Copy suggestion: revisions
- “Revisions” table:
  - Revision #, author, timestamp, changes summary
- This will reduce confusion in results when config changes.

6) Audit log tab
- Needs to match security audit events spec.
- Events: created, updated, validated, started, paused, resumed, ended, rolled back (auto), rolled back (manual), guardrail triggered.
- Display should include actor + reason.

Edge cases & policy precedence (notes from routing discussions)

Overlapping with canary rollouts
- Expected precedence (per current conversations; confirm with ADR-0187):
  - Reliability fallbacks (e.g., capacity / error fallback) should override experiment assignment.
  - Canary rollouts: unclear; product wants experiment to be “the” mechanism for comparing variants; platform notes canaries are also a form of traffic splitting.
- UI guidance
  - During validation: if route has an active canary policy, block start OR warn strongly.
  - Proposed: warn, not block, but require explicit acknowledgement checkbox: “I understand results may be confounded by concurrent rollouts.”

Paused experiment behavior
- Pause means:
  - No exposure logging? (Telemetry question)
    - Suggest: still log “eligible but not assigned due to paused”?? That might create noise. Better: no exposure events if split=0.
  - Results should show paused interval.

Retries / streaming reconnect
- Issue seen in early dogfood: assignment flipping on retries.
- UI copy: in “Stickiness” helper text mention “Retries are kept consistent when the same stickiness key is present.” (Assumes PR_18504 fix is shipped.)

Capacity / 429s and guardrails
- We should explicitly call out 429 as separate metric in Results because experiments can overload a smaller pool.
- SRE request: show a “Guardrail policies” section in review step:
  - “Auto-rollback if: error rate +X% vs baseline; p95 latency +Y% vs baseline; 429s exceed threshold”
  - Note: backend will likely implement absolute thresholds + relative deltas.

Copy/terminology alternatives (draft list)
- “End experiment” vs “Stop experiment” vs “Turn off”
  - Recommendation: “End experiment” (less ambiguous, matches audit).
- “Rollback”
  - Use only when we are actively reverting due to guardrails. Manual action could be “Rollback now” but it’s essentially “End and restore default policy.”
  - Alternative: “Revert traffic” (clearer).
- “Eligibility rules”
  - Header: “Where this experiment applies”
  - Rows: regions, projects, routes. Avoid “eligibility” jargon unless in advanced section.

UX nits / copy tweaks from dogfood (quick list)
- Users tried to click split chart thinking it edits; add explicit “Edit split” button.
- Variant naming
  - Allow custom display name (e.g., “llama-3.1-70b-q4” is too long). Show model ID as subtext.
  - Add suggested default names: “Variant A”, “Variant B” (not “Control/Treatment”).
- Confirmation modals should include the route name + split (to prevent accidents).

Telemetry constraints that affect UI (Paula/Logan notes)
- Avoid allowing free-form tags (high cardinality). UI should not prompt for “custom dimensions”.
- Exposure logging sampling
  - If sampling is <100%, results UI should show a badge: “Exposures sampled at 10%” and explain that volume metrics are estimated.

Proposed UI warnings library (states)
- Warning: “No stable stickiness identifier”
- Warning: “Conflicting rollout policy detected”
- Warning: “Variant under 5% allocation”
- Warning: “Region/model availability mismatch”
- Critical: “Route already has running experiment”
- Critical: “Insufficient permissions”

Concrete mock copy (draft)

Validation warnings panel
- Title: “Review warnings before starting”
- Warning 1: “Assignments may not be consistent”
  - Body: “This experiment is using API key–based assignment. End users may switch variants between requests. To keep a user on the same variant, configure a stable user identifier header.”
- Warning 2: “Concurrent rollouts detected”
  - Body: “This route has an active canary rollout. Experiment results may be difficult to interpret if multiple traffic-splitting policies are active.”

Guardrail banner (Running)
- Healthy: “Guardrails: healthy (no regressions detected)”
- At risk: “Guardrails: regression detected — monitoring (auto-rollback if sustained)”
- Rolled back: “Rolled back automatically due to guardrail violation (p95 latency +18% vs Variant A)”

Implementation notes / asks to Eng (for feasibility)
- Need an API field that clearly expresses experiment state transitions (Draft/Running/Paused/Ended/RolledBack) and timestamps.
- Need “effective routing” signal: whether a request assigned to variant was overridden by fallback (to avoid misattribution). Even if we can’t show in UI yet, note for reporting integrity.
- Need “config revision id” in exposure events (or at least in aggregation) if we allow edits mid-flight.

Next steps
- Kenji/Tessa: update DES-142 flow to remove default “Control” language and add warning panel placement.
- Chloe/Jada: confirm backend validation behavior for overlapping experiments/rollouts.
- Paula/Allison: confirm which guardrail metrics are guaranteed in v1 (p95 latency, error rate, 429 separate?).
- Dylan: decide whether we allow mid-flight split edits for Beta or require “end + duplicate”.

Appendix: quick decision log (informal)
- 2026-02-10: Remove “Control/Treatment” default naming. (Marissa + Design consensus)
- 2026-02-12: Add “Paused” state distinct from “Ended” (Design proposes; Eng to confirm state machine).
- 2026-02-18: Results page will include 429 chart separate from 5xx. (SRE request)
